newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INTERVIEW-Sateras sees majority of gains offshore.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Sateras sees majority of gains offshore.

text.p: Malaysian property developer Sateras Resources Bhd said on Friday it expected the bulk of its future profits to come from property and cement ventures in China and locally.
"Property development and the three cement plants we have in China will be the main contributors to the group," said managing director Mohamed Kamal Hussain.
Sateras owns two cement plants in Dalian, China. On Thursday, it announced the acquisition of a third plant in Malaysia's northeastern state of Kelantan for 800 million ringgit ($321 million).
Mohamed Kamal said Sateras was developing an 84-acre site in the southern port city of Johor Baru comprising a mixture of condominiums and commercial buildings.

Also in the pipeline was the development of a tropical forest resort in the Terengganu state which borders Kelantan. Construction of this project, located near Malaysia's national park, the Taman Negara, would commence in the next financial year, Mohamed Kamal said.

He said ventures in China, Australia, the South Pacific and Southeast Asia were expected to contribute around 60 percent of Sateras' group revenue after 1998. The overseas projects include automobile manufacturing, hotel management, computer software development and plywood making.
Sateras has signed an agreement with the authorities of China's Hefei city to manufacture around 300,000 cars per year, a project now under way.

Mohamed Kamal said another deal would be signed soon to acquire a 25 percent stake in a company owned by the Chinese Ministry of Finance to increase the production capacity to 600,000 units per year. The stake would cost Sateras around $50 million.
Mohamed Kamal said Sateras would shortly announce the acquisition of six hotels in Fiji, and one in the resort island of Bali in Indonesia. He did not give any details.

The Malaysian group has initiated a joint-venture with Australian-based Oxford Media Pty Ltd, which owns the patents for an electronic payment system known as Cybank. The product allows Internet-based transactions between vendors and customers who subscribe to the system.

Sateras has global marketing rights for the product, in which it has invested some 2.5 million ringgit. "It is the only one of its kind in the world and it has tremendous potential," said Mohamed Kamal.
In Fiji, Sateras would acquire a plywood manufacturer, which would see the group diversifying into the timber trade, Mohamed Kamal said.
The funding for these acquisitions would come from a mixture of share swaps and bank borrowings, he said.
"We go where there are opportunities," he said. "There is a lot stiffer competition here (in Malaysia)."
